topics.label: Introduction to the Complement Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, notes the complexity of complement nomenclature, and frames the scope of the lecture.

topics.label: Principles, Nomenclature, and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture of the complement cascade, explaining its general logic, naming conventions, and the pivotal activation of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three recognition pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—that initiate complement convertase activity and deposit C3b on target surfaces.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of the Complement Cascade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector processes triggered by complement activation, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane attack complex lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins that protect host cells from unintended complement deposition and destruction.

topics.label: Clinical Presentations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how deficiencies in individual complement components produce distinct immunodeficiency and autoimmune manifestations.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens evolve specific mechanisms to circumvent complement clearance, highlighting Staphylococcus aureus and clinical uses of Protein A.

topics.label: Conclusion and Next Lecture Preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
